page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c28g1.14xlarge is a dedicated GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 processor architecture. This configuration delivers 56 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 224.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. In addition to high-density host compute and memory, the instance integrates two NVIDIA P4 graphics processing units providing an aggregate of 16 GB of dedicated GPU video memory.

Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth capacity of 10 Gbps to support heavy data transfers between cloud infrastructure endpoints. The instance does not include bundled local storage, meaning primary operating system volumes and application datasets require network-attached block storage devices. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default, requiring allocation of standard cloud networking interfaces for external ingress or egress traffic.

Hardware resource distribution suits tasks that couple substantial multi-threaded host processing with hardware-accelerated processing pipelines. Given the dual NVIDIA P4 graphics architecture and 56 dedicated vCPUs, suitable workloads include distributed deep learning inference, video transcoding, visual computing, rendering, and computer vision data pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c28g1.14xlarge is an x86_64 GPU-accelerated instance designed for visual processing and machine learning inference. Provisioned via the KVM hypervisor, it provides 56 dedicated vCPUs and 224.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Hardware acceleration is provided by two discrete NVIDIA P4 GPUs totaling 16 GB of GDDR5 VRAM. Network communication operates at a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes no onboard local storage, necessitating external cloud block volumes for operational data persistence, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. This instance profile serves computationally demanding environments such as concurrent video transcoding, neural network inference, and visual rendering pipelines requiring high vCPU concurrency alongside dedicated GPU acceleration.
